traceability.notes:
The story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING is fully implemented and verified: - Every relevant rule defines clear, specific, and consistent error message templates using ESLint’s `meta.messages` with placeholders (e.g., `{{name}}`, `{{functionName}}`, `{{missing}}`, `{{details}}`, `{{path}}`, `{{reqId}}`, `{{storyPath}}`). - Tests assert not only that errors are raised, but that the correct `messageId` and `data` payloads are provided, and in the case of `require-story-annotation` they also verify ESLint suggestions (desc + fix function) are wired correctly. - File and requirement reference rules distinguish between missing entities and filesystem/configuration failures, reporting appropriate, contextual messages and never throwing uncaught errors. - Error severities align with ESLint best practices (rules are `type: 'problem'` and `recommended: 'error'` where appropriate), and annotation format issues are reported as problems but are clearly labeled and, when safe, auto-fixable. - All tests that reference this story and its requirements pass under the current test run.
Given this concrete evidence across rule implementations, focused test suites, and a clean test run, all acceptance criteria and requirements for docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md are satisfied.
